notes:
## 0.5.3

- A combine reply that stays cut off now keeps all completed summary parts, including sections and action items. A failed attempt reports saved parts only when it saved them during that attempt, and a summary made in one part records the model it used.

- Settings is reorganised and searchable. It opens on a search box (Ctrl+F) and seven sections: Dictation, Writing, AI & privacy, Shortcuts, General, Advanced, and About & help. Each setting now lives in one place, the same in every theme, and picking a search result takes you straight to it. Format lists and Format numbers are now one switch. The Shortcuts tab is now the Shortcuts section, Restore previous clipboard is on the History page, and Report a problem is in About & help.
- Restore previous clipboard now shows on the History page only while there is a saved copy to restore; with none, the card is gone. A restore that finishes cleanly hides it and says so; any other result, such as newer contents kept or an error, stays on the card until the next check. Searching for it still opens History, and takes you to the card when there is one.
- In Meetings, when Cloud cleanup is off, the summary and Ask pages now say so and the button opens the Cloud cleanup setting instead of the Groq key.
- Meeting summaries on Groq's free plan wait far less. Dicta now sends a meeting in as few requests as your Groq account allows: one when it fits, otherwise the largest parts that fit, instead of one request per topic. An hour-long meeting takes about four requests instead of a dozen or more, and waits only as long as Groq's limit says.
- While a summary waits for Groq, it shows about how long is left ("about 3 min left on Groq's free plan") instead of "continuing in 60 s". Stop still works.
- Fixed: a long meeting's summary could fail with "Groq returned an error (HTTP 400)". Dicta now gives the model enough room to finish its reply, asks once more when the reply comes back cut off, keeps what was complete, and splits a request Groq calls too long. When Groq still refuses, the message says why.
- A long meeting's summary no longer loses everything when it fails or you stop it. The parts it finished show under "Completed parts from the last attempt" on the Summary tab until a new summary is made.
- Meeting indicator windows are destroyed 10 seconds after notes stop, releasing their WebView2 memory; a quick restart reuses them.
- Meetings now tell the people on a call apart. After a call, the transcript shows Speaker 1, Speaker 2 and so on instead of one "Them". This runs on your PC: no audio or transcript leaves it. Separate speakers is on by default; its model (about 47 MB) downloads automatically when the first call meeting ends, or when you turn the switch on, with progress and Stop on the meeting page and in Settings; turning the switch off cancels the download. Click a speaker to rename them, pick "Same person as" when one person was split in two, or Undo merge to restore their label and name. Reruns keep names when speech overlap identifies a unique match; a manual rerun warns when names or merges exist. A single speaker inherits a renamed "Them". Names carry into the copied and exported transcript, summaries and Ask. Automatic summaries wait for separation; if it fails or you stop it, the summary still runs. A quit during separation or its download leaves the summary pending for the next launch. Older calls whose audio is still kept get a Separate speakers button. Turn it off with Separate speakers in Settings > General, which also has Remove model.
